temporal_state_chain.observed: Ethan notices Gary working excessively long hours at the hospital, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep. Ethan invites Gary to a weekend retreat, but Gary declines because he has too much to do at the hospital.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary is dedicated but overworking due to hospital demands and that a relaxing retreat could help him regain perspective.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes. Gary's refusal shows he feels unable or unwilling to step away because of hospital obligations.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Gary is heavily bound by hospital work and may resist taking a break, even when his health is at risk.
temporal_state_chain.intention: Continue supporting Gary and encouraging him to take steps toward rest and better health.

temporal_state_chain.observed: During the retreat, Ethan sees Gary behaving restlessly and avoiding discussions about work. When Ethan confronts him, Gary says his situation is complicated and that he did not want to burden Ethan.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary's overwork is mainly caused by hospital demands, though he has noticed Gary is not relaxing as expected.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes. Gary's restlessness and evasiveness, along with saying it is complicated, lead Ethan to suspect there is more than professional pressure behind Gary's behavior.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Gary is likely hiding deeper personal or emotional burdens related to his overwork, and he may need a nonjudgmental friend to open up to.
temporal_state_chain.intention: Confront Gary gently, encourage him to share what is really going on, and offer nonjudgmental help.

temporal_state_chain.observed: Gary opens up about the pressures of managing a new department and personal challenges he is facing. He accepts Ethan's suggestion to prioritize tasks and delegate responsibilities.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary has deeper stress beyond routine hospital work, but he does not yet know the specific reasons.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes. Learning the actual pressures and personal challenges gives Ethan a clearer understanding of why Gary has been overworking.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Gary's overwork is understandable and can be improved through practical changes like prioritizing tasks, delegating, and organizing his schedule.
temporal_state_chain.intention: Help Gary organize his responsibilities and find a healthier work-life balance.

temporal_state_chain.observed: Over the following months, Ethan regularly checks in with Gary. Gary reports that he is doing better, feels less overwhelmed, and even had time for a movie.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary is working toward improvement but still faces challenges and benefits from regular encouragement.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes. Gary's reported progress and visible efforts confirm that Ethan's support is helping and that Gary is genuinely improving.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Gary is making meaningful progress toward a healthier work-life balance and is becoming less overwhelmed.
temporal_state_chain.intention: Continue checking in with Gary, offering support and encouragement as he maintains his progress.

temporal_state_chain.observed: After a year, Gary has successfully adjusted to a healthier work-life balance. Gary thanks Ethan and says he feels much more in control and capable of managing on his own.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary has made significant progress but may still benefit from periodic support.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes. Gary's sustained adjustment and self-sufficiency show that he can now manage without Ethan's active intervention.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Gary no longer needs close support to maintain his balance; Ethan can step back while remaining available if needed.
temporal_state_chain.intention: Step back, let Gary maintain his independence, and remain available if Gary ever needs help again.
